findings.title: KeyError on integration.metadata["sender"] when metadata has no sender
findings.body: `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` reaches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` whenever an `Integration` row exists for the `installation_id` but no `OrganizationIntegration` rows exist. `metadata["sender"]` is only populated by `build_integration` when the pipeline/webhook state contains `sender` (see `build_integration`: `if state.get("sender")`), and integrations created through the normal pipeline do not have it — `tests/.../test_integration.py::test_basic_flow` asserts the saved metadata contains only access_token/expires_at/icon/domain_name/account_type. So for any integration whose OrganizationIntegration was hard-deleted (e.g. org deletion) or that was created without a sender, a re-install attempt raises `KeyError: 'sender'` and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide explicitly what to do when the sender is unknown.

findings.title: OAuth `state` is the deterministic pipeline signature, so the state check gives no CSRF protection
findings.body: The authorize redirect uses `state = pipeline.signature` and the callback only checks `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`. The pipeline signature is deterministic and not user/session specific — the new tests hardcode the same value `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` for different users and organizations (`test_github_installed_on_another_org`, `test_github_user_mismatch`, `test_github_prevent_install_until_pending_deletion_is_complete`). An attacker can therefore construct a callback URL with a valid `state` plus their own `code`, and if a victim with an in-flight pipeline loads it, the attacker's GitHub identity gets bound into the victim's pipeline via `github_authenticated_user` — exactly the class of attack this PR is meant to prevent. The state should be a per-pipeline random nonce stored in pipeline state and compared on return.

findings.title: Authenticated GitHub user is not verified when the Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist` the pipeline advances immediately (`return pipeline.next_step()`) without any comparison of `github_authenticated_user` against the account that installed the app. The sender information this check relies on is written by the asynchronous `installation` webhook, so whether the validation runs at all depends on webhook delivery timing: an attacker who knows a victim's `installation_id` and completes the redirect before the webhook is processed bypasses the new check entirely. The installation ownership should be verified against the authenticated user's own token (e.g. `GET /user/installations`) rather than relying on a pre-existing Integration row.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange / get_user_info produce a 500 instead of the error page
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are called without exception handling. `get_user_info` performs an HTTP request and raises `ApiError`/`ApiHostError` on non-2xx or network failures (e.g. revoked token, GitHub outage, rate limiting), and `safe_urlopen` raises on connection errors. Only the JSON/body parse is wrapped in `try/except`. The result is an unhandled 500 in the install popup rather than the intended `github-integration-failed.html` page, with no log line to diagnose it. Wrap both calls and fall back to `error(request, self.active_organization)` (plus a log).

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 installation path
findings.body: This test previously asserted `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."`, covering the `ApiError(404) -> IntegrationError` branch in `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration`. It now passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, a different value from the `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` signature used by every other test in this file, and asserts only the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`. The request therefore short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView` on the state mismatch and the 404 handling in `build_integration` is no longer covered by any test. Either restore the correct state so the flow reaches `build_integration`, or add a separate test for the invalid-state branch and keep a real installation-not-found test.

findings.title: gettext applied to a runtime variable breaks string extraction for the short error messages
findings.body: `error()` wraps its `error_short` argument at call time with `_(error_short)`. Because the argument is a variable rather than a literal inside the `_()` call, `makemessages` cannot extract strings like "GitHub installation pending deletion." or "Github installed on another Sentry organization." anymore (previously they were literals inside `_()`), so these user-facing strings will silently stop being translated. Pass already-lazy/translated values from the call sites instead of translating the variable.
